findings.comment: chardet.detect can detect encodings that iconv-lite does not support (such as UTF-32LE, UTF-32BE, or unsupported code pages). Passing an unsupported encoding to iconv.decode will throw an unhandled 'Encoding not recognized' error and crash open().

jschardet reports UTF-8 as 'UTF-8' (with a hyphen) and plain ASCII files as 'ascii'. Checking fileEncoding.toLowerCase() !== 'utf8' evaluates to true for 'utf-8', causing redundant disk writes on all UTF-8 files. More seriously, files detected as 'ascii' will be re-encoded with iconv.encode(..., 'ascii'), which corrupts any non-ASCII characters added during editing into question marks (?). Additionally, writing directly to disk after showTextDocument has opened the document can cause editor desync or file change conflicts.

Reading the entire file into a buffer before checking its size defeats the size limit check. For large files (e.g. multi-gigabyte files), this can cause significant memory pressure or crash the process with ERR_FS_FILE_TOO_LARGE. The file size should be inspected prior to reading the buffer (and getFileSizeInKB, imported on line 7, is now left unused).

isBinaryFile is only checked inside the else branch when chardet.detect returns no encoding. However, jschardet almost always detects an encoding (such as windows-1252 or ISO-8859-2) for arbitrary binary files like images, executables, and archives. As a result, the else branch is never reached, binary detection is bypassed, and binary files will be decoded as text and returned instead of throwing the expected error.

jschardet can detect encodings that iconv-lite does not support (e.g. UTF-32LE, UTF-32BE, ISO-2022-KR, EUC-TW). When an unsupported encoding name is passed to iconv.decode, iconv-lite throws an unhandled error ('Encoding not recognized'). Additionally, jschardet.detect returns an IDetectResult object, never a string, making typeof detected === 'string' dead code.
